ASSESSMENT OF WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT ACROSS RIVER BASINS: A COMPARATIVE FRAMEWORK

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: M. Luckmanul Chakim, Sri Wahyuni, Pitojo Tri Juwono, Hari Siswoyo
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.03.2026.604.613

ABSTRACT

Performance assessment in river basin management often relies on sectoral indicators, even though basin managers work across ecological restoration, water-service delivery, infrastructure operation, and disaster-risk control at the same time. This article develops a comparative index framework for benchmarking water resources management performance in ten Indonesian river basins that have implemented Water Resources Management Service Fees (WRMSF/BJPSDA). The framework separates performance indicators from contextual explanatory variables and aggregates three management pillars: conservation, water utilization, and water-related destructive control. Indicators are first oriented as benefit or cost variables, normalized with a min-max transformation, averaged at the pillar level, and then synthesized into a Composite Basin Performance Index (CBPI). The Brantas (0.839) and Citarum (0.817) river basins are performing high based on equally weighted benchmarks. On the other hand, Cimanuk-Cisanggarung (0.534) and Seputih-Sekampung (0.554) are included in the low performance category. The other six river basins are in the medium performance category, with scores that are close together. The analysis at the pillar level indicates that the composite score should not be viewed as a simple rank-ordering. The sensitivity analysis showed that the top position for Brantas and Citarum remains unchanged, but the ranks of some river basins within the medium performance group may change if more importance is given to conservation, utilization or destructive force control. The proposed CBPI is a transparent and reusable tool for comparing river basins, setting priorities and supporting performance-based funding, while allowing for contextual interpretation to ensure rankings are not viewed in an overly simplistic manner.
